hints.content: **Reflective (or line) symmetry** means that we can reflect a figure across a line, and the figure will remain unchanged.

##Reflection over $\overline{BD}$

Under this transformation, some points on the pentagon map to another point which is no longer on the pentagon.  


[[☃ image 1]]

The pentagon is *not symmetric* over this line.

options.alt: A regular pentagon A B C D E where all the sides are congruent. A blue horizontal line connects from points D to B on the opposite side. The image of the pentagon reflected across the blue line does not fit on the pre-image.

hints.content:
##Reflection over $\overline{AC}$

Under this transformation, some points on the pentagon map to another point which is no longer on the pentagon.  


[[☃ image 1]]

The pentagon is *not symmetric* over this line.

options.alt: A regular pentagon A B C D E where all the sides are congruent. A blue slanted line connects from points C to A. The image of the pentagon reflected across the blue line does not fit on the pre-image.

hints.content:
Neither symmetry applies to the pentagon.

Symmetry | Applies to the figure?
:- | :-:
Reflective symmetry over $\overline{BD}$ | No
Reflective symmetry over $\overline{AC}$ | No
